paper.title: Algorithm 835: MultRoot - A Matlab package for computing polynomial roots and multiplicities
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 30(2), 218-236 (June 2004); Collected Algorithms from ACM, Algorithm 835. ACM article not read (dl.acm.org 403 from this host); code and readme from the netlib archive.

stack: MATLAB/Octave (TOMS 835 Matlab/Src multroot.m, run under GNU Octave 10.3.0 from conda-forge; MATLAB is proprietary and was not used)

claim.text: multroot(f) on the readme's worked example f = poly([ones(1,20),2*ones(1,20),3*ones(1,10),4*ones(1,5)]) returns multiplicities 5, 10, 20, 20 for roots 4, 3, 2, 1 (exact), and the roots within 1e-9 absolute of the printed values. The registered claim's values are split per root here: same numbers and tolerances, one numeric value per root so the gates can judge them.

reference.archive: netlib.org/toms/835.gz, sha256 ce26ae432aeb7009b30e066a4da73092baaacc7fc2525668646fd307adfdb8ff (fetched 2026-11-27); the file is the archive's Doc/readme.txt, section 3 holds the printed table

attempt: Ran the authors' Matlab/Src/multroot.m as shipped (no source edit), on the readme's worked example, under Octave 10.3.0. Octave's own m-library is not on the default load path of this conda build, so the first run (no path step) stops at 'poly' undefined: that is the original attempt, kept in evidence/original-attempt-octave-nopath.log. The harness impl/run_example.m adds Octave's m-library and the authors' directories with addpath, then calls multroot exactly as the readme does. Three recipe passes: multiplicities 5,10,20,20 in all of them; roots differ by at most 4e-14 between passes because multroot's helpers uminsv.m and zminsv.m draw an unseeded rand() start vector (authors' code; not seeded here). Largest deviation from the printed roots across passes: 6e-14 (root 4), far inside 1e-9. The readme's own condition number 73.6821 also reproduced (not a registered value).

original_attempt.reason: octave-cli 10.3.0 with the authors' directories on the path but without the step that loads Octave's own m-library: 'poly' undefined. The authors' code was never reached; the fault is the conda build's load path, not the artifact. The harness addpath is the workaround.
